# read_B: pp. 57–59 (leaves n58–n60), established from the images

Line counts: p. 57 has five lines (a leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔, checked). p. 58 has five lines (a leaf back, no ornament, checked). p. 59 has five lines (a leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔, checked). That makes 15 print lines.
The witness's line breaks match the print on every line (15 of 15).

Method: line bands were located from the row profile (headlines n58 at y≈160/215/270/320/370, n59 ≈135/192/248/302/358, n60 ≈140/196/250/306/362). Each line was cropped in four (n58) or five (n59, n60) overlapping segments at ×3 (LANCZOS). Every doubtful syllable was cropped at ×6–×10, mostly side by side with a known form of the same letter from the same page. For 59.1 the pixels were also dumped. The scan is bilevel and the tshegs are small. A tsheg is judged absent only where the letters touch or there is clear empty space with no dot.

## [?] (2)

- 57.2 དྲག་བོས[?]: the letter after དྲག་ is a box with o. At ×7–×10, side by side with the པ of པའི and the བ of བར in the same line, it shows a thin white slit near the top right, which is more like the open corner of པ. The difference is a pixel or two, and the vowel stem falls just there. The witness has བོས, and the print writes བ for པ elsewhere (57.3 གྲུབ་བས, 58.1 རིམ་བ, 54.1 རྣམ་བར), so the witness is taken. Sense: དྲག་པོས "fierce" (as in 51.4 and 57.4 དྲག་པོས of this print).
- 58.3 ཡུན་རིང་[?]༔: after རིང there is a wide blank (about 25 px) before ༔. The head stroke of ང runs on to the right and ends in a round knob, which may be a tsheg fused to the headline or just the end of the stroke. The witness has རིང་༔, and that is taken. The blank is a gap in the block and is not written.

Close calls not marked [?]:
- 57.4 (line end) ལམ་: a row of dots follows མ, the first about 16 px from the letter. It is taken as the tsheg, as C did (the witness agrees).
- 59.4 སྤྱོད: the ya-btags tail is short but present. With ཡ-less སྤོད being no word, it is not marked.
- Other line-end tshegs (57.2, 57.3, 57.5, 58.2, 58.4, 59.2, 59.3) are visible as a dot before the frame or as the first of the dots. They are kept. 58.3 and 59.4 end in ༔.

```
# fix: ཞན་ཡང་གཅིགལ་ངོས => ཞན་ཡང་གཅིག་ལ་ངོས
# fix: མི་སྲིདདོ => མི་སྲིད་དོ
# fix: དག་སྣངདང => དག་སྣང་དང
# fix: སོ་སོའིསྣང་བ => སོ་སོའི་སྣང་བ
```
- 58.1→58.2 and 59.1→59.2: there is no tsheg at the line end. Neither join crosses a page-opening ornament.
- 58.5→59.1 (འོང་ | ༄༅༔ ༔སྐོ༔) has its tsheg. The ornament join is for the drafter, as usual.
- 58.2 and 58.3 are mid-line joins with no tsheg (the headlines run on).
- No line-end abbreviations or contractions (པའཾ, ལཾ, ནམཁའ, subscript-ས) occur on these pages.

## Suspected misprints (kept as printed)

1. **59.1 ༔སྐོ༔ for ངོ༔.** p. 58 ends …ཤར་ནས་འོང་, and the formula is འོང་ངོ༔ (as at 53.2 and 54.1, the "comes" + -o of 59.5 འོང་ངོ་༔, and the other recension here: འཆར་ནས་འོང་ངོ་༔). The letters as cut are ས over ྐ with naro, which makes no sense here. A ངོ miscut in the block (or recut at the leaf turn) is the only reading that fits. The certainty that a fix is needed is high. That the cut letters are སྐོ is fairly certain (a pixel-level comparison with སྐད), but a worn or damaged ངོ cannot be fully excluded. Proposed `# fix: ༔སྐོ༔ དེ་ངོ => ༔ངོ༔ དེ་ངོ`, with the print's reading in the note. If the drafter prefers to treat it as illegible, write ངོ[?].
2. **59.5 ཞེས་ཁྱ་བ for ཞེས་བྱ་བ** ("called"). The certainty is high: the sense allows only བྱ, and the other recension has ཞེས་བྱ་བ. The letter is plainly ཁ (see above). Proposed `# fix: ཞེས་ཁྱ་བ => ཞེས་བྱ་བ`.
3. 57.2 དྲག་བོས[?] and 57.3 གྲུབ་བས: the print's བ-for-པ habit. Note only.
4. 58.5 དུས་ཅིག་ལ (for གཅིག; the same line has དུས་གཅིག་ལ). It is the indefinite form, and the sense is the same ("at one time"). Kept, note only.
5. 58.1 ཞན་ཡང (other recension ཞན་ཀྱང): ཡང as a concessive after ན is acceptable. Kept, note only.

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: མཚེར (57.1), རིམ་བ (58.1), དངངས (58.4, 59.2), ཕྱི་ལ་ཁྲིད (58.3).
